newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore products mixed on weaker crude.
newsitem.headline: Singapore products mixed on weaker crude.

text.p: Singapore oil products closed mixed with gas oil and jet fuel still holding on to its earlier gains despite weaker crude values, traders said on Friday.
Gas oil was bid around $29.80 a barrel, just under the $30.00 five-year record traded on Thursday, and offers are unchanged at above $30.00.
Market is firm on renewed buying from China which bought more than 100,000-tonnes over the past few days with the most recent trade at $232 per tonne cost-and-freight, traders said.
Buying also seen from Indonesia which is not able to operate one of its Cilacap crude unit at full capacity, they said.
Gas oil supplies in the Gulf is tight with a cargo traded earlier at $1.05 premium to Middle East quotes. Traders said most producers there are sold out for October loading cargoes.
Jet fuel was unchanged in quiet trade with a major offering at $30.10 fob Singapore.
High sulphur fuel oil prices eased as bearish cash fundamentals override the effects of crude gains to cause levels to move lower.
A local trader purchased a cargo of 20,000 tonnes of 180 cst at $121 for loading October 26-30 from a European major. The same trader was seeking two cargoes of 380-cst at $115.50.

Naphtha dip on weaker overnight crude, but buyers remained sidelined in anticipation of a weaker market. Market assessed firm, with India's Reliance to buy 50,000 tonnes for November for a new 700,000 tonne a year ethylene plant. North Asian petrochemical plants return from shutdown. Supplies in Singapore were tight with only a cargo available for mid-November. Taiwan bought its November heavy naphtha cargo at $230 a tonne, $30 over its October purchase, despite earlier talk of cancelling it. Gasoline was steady with a Japanese trader keeping its bid for 50,000 barrels of 92-oct unleaded at $24.45 for November 1-5 lifting. -- Singapore newsroom (65-870-3093)
